To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Taylor-Hood pair is not stable with respect to the mesh aspect ratio and (b) the Taylor-H Hood pair can be stabilized with respect to the aspect ratio by using the Brezzi-Falk-Winther pair for the pressure space.
the Taylor-Hood pair is unstable for anisotropic elements, but the Taylor-Hood scheme is stable for a certain class of anisotropic elements.

the following velocity-pressure pairs are stable with respect to growing anisotropy of the elements: the Taylor-Hood pair, the Scott-Vogelius pair, the Crouzeix-Raviart pair, the Bercovier-Pironneau pair and the Bercovieri-Engelman pair.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1. stability of the velocity-pressure pairs with the standard pressure space on anisotropic elements, 2. stability of velocity-pressure pairs with anisotropic pressure spaces, 3. numerical tests of several discretizations on anisotropic grids.
discretizations of the stationary Stokes equations on anisotropic triangular or quadrilateral meshes.
the question, which discretizations are stable on meshes with anisotropic elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability properties of discretizations of Stokes problems are very much mesh dependent.
there are no stable discretizations on anisotropic grids for the Stokes problem.
there is no discretization of the Stokes problem that is stable on anisotropic elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a velocity-pressure pair should be stable on anisotropic elements if the velocity space is a subspace of the pressure gradient space.
the stability of a velocity-pressure pair is not affected by anisotropic mesh elements if the pair is stable in the sense of the discrete inf-sup condition.
the velocity-pressure pair (H(div),L2) is the most robust with respect to the anisotropy of the elements in an unstructured mesh.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of a velocity-pressure pair with respect to growing anisotropy of elements in the mesh is not a sufficient condition for the pair to yield a convergent approximation to the solution.

the stability of the discretization depends on the aspect ratio of the mesh elements, and the velocity-pressure pairs which are stable on isotropic meshes are not stable for large aspect ratios of the mesh elements.

, in general, a discretization of the Stokes problem is stable with respect to anisotropy of the mesh, if it is stable on isotropic meshes and the pressure is approximated on a mesh which is sufficiently fine with respect to the mesh for the velocity.
